Preferences

Preferences holds MixOS's preference editors in one window. The flat sidebar lists Appearance, Text & Fonts, Windows, Apps (Email, Term, Ced), Accessibility, and Software & Updates. Hairlines separate look, desktop, apps and system pages. Empty categories are hidden. Each page starts with an Affects: line. Wallpaper opens from Appearance.

Section commands have no default shortcuts. The Apps header is a plain label.

Press / outside a text field, or choose the magnifier in the title bar's icon bar, to focus search. It filters sections by title, category, extra words and settings keys, ignoring case. Try terminal. or background. Enter opens the first match. Escape clears search and releases focus. Ctrl+/ opens Keyboard shortcuts.

Software & Updates

Software shows its followed apps, from the releases service: each app's installed version, the latest release, when it was published, and its status (up to date, update available, not installed, not checked, or check failed).

  • Check for updates (Ctrl+Shift+R) asks GitHub about every followed app.
  • Update group installs newer releases for installed apps in the selected group.
  • Select an app to see its latest release notes, then:
    • Install or update (Ctrl+I) installs it, or updates it if it is installed;
    • Roll back returns to the previous version;
    • Remove… asks first; Cancel is the default, so Enter never removes.
  • Refresh (Ctrl+R) reads the list again without asking GitHub.

The group selector at the top offers MixOS Desktop, MixOS Server and Creative applications. A catalogue entry's optional category selects mixos-desktop, mixos-server, creative or other; application names and publishers remain catalogue data. The catalogue's top-level categories map can label a group, for example categories: {creative: "Graphics"}. Unrecognised catalogue entries remain accessible in Other, which appears only when it has rows. Changing groups clears the previous selection and its release notes; selecting an app through the Bus opens its group automatically.

One operation runs at a time; the status bar says what is happening and how it ended. Installs are per user, verified against the checksums each release publishes, and the previous version is kept for rolling back: see Application releases.

If the releases service is not running, the editor says so instead of an empty list. You follow apps by listing them in ~/.config/mixos/releases.mx.

Appearance

Appearance sets the session's colour scheme, light or dark mode, contrast, Widget style, and Density through settingsd. Widget style controls how buttons, fields and panels are drawn; a scheme brings its own style unless you pick one. Density offers Compact (0.85), Comfortable (1.0), and Spacious (1.2), scaling spacing and control heights. Off-step values remain stored and show Custom (x). Wallpaper opens its existing editor from this page.

Windows holds title bars (Automatic, Drawn by the app, Drawn by the system) and window-button side. Automatic shows its current result; button side is editable when the effective title bar is drawn by the app.

Each change applies to the whole session as you make it, as in GNOME's settings: the apps that follow the session look (Prefs itself, Workshop, and the portal's clients) change with it. Only the setting you changed is written. Changes made quickly one after another are sent in turn, never lost.

If settingsd refuses a change, Preferences keeps it and says so: Apply (Ctrl+S) tries again and Revert drops it. If the appearance is changed elsewhere at the same moment (another window, or an agent), Preferences follows it on every setting you did not touch. If it changed one you did, Preferences names it and applies nothing until you choose Keep my changes or Revert. Every change is checked against the revision you were shown, so it never lands on a change you have not seen. If its answer is lost, Preferences asks settingsd for the change's receipt before anything else is applied (Check again asks now); if settingsd no longer holds one, the session's current state decides what the status line says.

Text & Fonts

Text & Fonts shows the interface, heading and monospace faces currently installed on the window, with previews. Interface and monospace family pickers list installed families, sorted without duplicates; the monospace picker lists only families with monospaced faces. The font list is read once in the background. The first row restores the design default (Inter or JetBrains Mono), stored as null. A stored family absent from the list stays visible, marked missing. Interface weight and size controls sit beside the family choices. The size reset restores Design default, stored as null; an unset size is labelled with the design's pixel size. Viewing or tabbing through controls does not save a value.

Family choices use the same fenced drafts and conflict handling as Appearance. The toolkit currently installs bundled Inter and JetBrains Mono regardless of those stored names, including after a theme reload or restart. Other families take effect when the toolkit supports loading them; this stage adds no font loader. The faces grid and previews show the actual egui font stacks, rather than the saved request.

Accessibility

Larger text (50–300%, in 5% steps) multiplies every text size, including readers, editors and the terminal grid. Reset restores 100%. Reduce motion reduces animation in apps and the compositor. Related rows open Contrast in Appearance and Text size in Text & Fonts.

Apps

Apps → Term groups font family, size, weight and padding under Text; scrollback, scroll speed, cursor and copy on select under Behaviour; TERM, pane border and focus ring under Advanced. An unset family says Same as Monospace (…), following appearance.mono_family. Reset terminal and existing apply behaviour remain available.

Apps → Ced holds the editor's font, size, padding and light content. Email's Reading and Writing cards live on Apps → Email. Content sizes remain absolute in this step; no settings keys change.

Email

Apps → Email holds the email app's accounts and mail options (email.* in settingsd; see the email settings).

  • Accounts lists the accounts in the order Email's folder tree shows them, marking the default and any that are disabled. Add account opens a blank form; Move up and Move down reorder; Make default picks the account new mail is sent from (with none, the first enabled account); Remove… asks first, and Cancel is the default.
  • The selected account's form holds its name, JMAP URL (https, no trailing slash), login email, an optional CA bundle (an absolute PEM path; blank trusts the system roots) and a signature. Typing stays in the form until Save; Revert drops it. Each field is checked by the settings service's own rules first, and a field it would refuse is named under the field and nothing is sent. Enabled applies at once.
  • Mail holds messages per page (10 to 500), marking messages read when opened, and asking before deleting them; each applies at once. Reset email settings… asks first, then puts every email setting back to its default, which means no accounts.

Each change is one write to settingsd carrying the whole account list, and the default account in the same write when the change touches it (removing the default account clears it). Every write is checked against the revision shown, as on the Appearance panel. If settingsd refuses one, the status line gives its reason and the panel keeps showing what settingsd holds; your typing stays in the form.

Passwords never go to the settings service, whose settings every Bus client can read, and Preferences neither keeps nor shows them. Set password hands the typed password to Email itself (email.account.password.set), which keeps it in its own private file, and empties the field; the field gets the password back only if Email refuses it. If Email is not running, Preferences starts it (apps.launch) and waits up to about 16 seconds for it to come onto the Bus. Under the field, Preferences says whether Email holds a password for the account, as Email reports it (email.accounts), or that this is unknown because Email is not running. Connect now asks Email to connect the account (email.account.connect). Forget password… asks first (Cancel is the default), then has Email delete the password it keeps; it is the only time Preferences sends an empty password, and it starts Email if needed, as Set password does. Remove… goes through Email when it may be running (email.account.remove): Email removes the account from settingsd and forgets its password itself, and refuses while the account is still being migrated from its old configuration (MIGRATION_PENDING, shown as Email gives it). When Email is not running, Preferences removes the account from settingsd directly and, once settingsd shows it gone, asks a running Email to forget the password; Preferences does not start Email for this, and if Email is away or refuses, the status line says the password may still be held. An account still being migrated comes back when Email next starts, by design. An Email too old to know these commands is reported as such, not retried.

-- What Preferences shows: accounts (with has_password), default, mail options.
send prefs prefs.email

-- Add an account; the answer carries its new id.
send prefs prefs.email.set body='{"op":"add","name":"Work","url":"https://mail.example.com","email":"admin@example.com"}'

-- Change one field, make it the default, move it, disable it.
send prefs prefs.email.set body='{"op":"update","id":"acct-0f3a2b1c9d8e","signature":"-- Admin"}'
send prefs prefs.email.set body='{"op":"default","id":"acct-0f3a2b1c9d8e"}'
send prefs prefs.email.set body='{"op":"move","id":"acct-0f3a2b1c9d8e","direction":"up"}'
send prefs prefs.email.set body='{"op":"enable","id":"acct-0f3a2b1c9d8e","enabled":false}'

-- A mail option.
send prefs prefs.email.set body='{"path":"email.mail.page_size","value":50}'

-- Hand a password to Email (answered once Email has), or forget it.
send prefs prefs.email.password body='{"id":"acct-0f3a2b1c9d8e","password":"…"}'
send prefs prefs.email.password body='{"id":"acct-0f3a2b1c9d8e","forget":true}'

prefs.email.set takes op add, update, remove, move, default or enable, or path and value for a mail option. Over the Bus, remove removes at once: the confirmation belongs to the window. A field the settings service would refuse is answered with ARGUMENT, naming it. For scripts that do not need Preferences open, call settings.apply on the email.* paths directly, and email.account.password.set on Email.

For agents

Preferences answers on the Bus as prefs. prefs.info reports the whole state; prefs.apps the rows, selection and notes; prefs.appearance the session look, the expected look while a change settles, any held or conflicting edits and the revision read; prefs.appearance.set changes it at once (scheme, style with own for the scheme's own, mode, contrast, decorations, caption_side, window_style, menu_style, menu_side, title_align, actions_align, actions_place, font_family, mono_family, text_scale, density, reduced_motion). Family values are strings or null; text scale and density reset with 1.0, and reduced motion takes a boolean. Desktop → Windows places the window style picker beside caption placement. Its choices and labels come from the design registry; compd applies the chosen server-side furniture live. Title alignment's style default follows this choice. The same section offers Menus (Menu bar, Menu button, In the title bar) and Menu button (Left, Centre, Right). The side picker is enabled when menus are collapsed. In the title bar uses compd's button in SSD mode and the app's button in CSD mode. An offline or aliased app keeps its own menu button in SSD mode too. Title and Window buttons offer Style default, Left, Centre and Right. Actions offers In the app or In the title bar; Action icons offers Left, Centre and Right. These settings share one layout in CSD and SSD. Titlebar Action Bars use the same live registration agreement as menus; unregistered apps keep their own bar. The section ids in tree order are appearance, text_and_fonts, wallpaper, windows, apps_email, apps_term, apps_ced, accessibility, and software. Navigation actions use view.section.<id>; retired section ids have no aliases. Search includes their ui.* keys and both font-family keys. prefs.appearance and prefs.appearance.set are version 0.3.0. prefs.info version 0.5.0 and prefs.apps version 0.3.0 add release_status (Software's progress, install result or refusal text) and release_failed (whether that outcome failed). These stay separate from settings feedback in status and failed; a quiet release read preserves the last operation's outcome. The reply includes problem (the unresolved settings failure, or null) and problem_source (its page id, or null). Problems appear on their own page, with a link from other pages. A refused edit stays until its owner's next successful write or until the person dismisses it with × on that page. Reverting or retiring a look draft clears its look problem. A settings-service outage also clears on a recovered read. Email account tasks report their outcome inline and never create settings problems. prefs.section {name[, group]} opens a registry section. app.describe lists the section ids and their searchable metadata. For Software, group selects mixos-desktop, mixos-server, creative or other. prefs.select {app} opens the app's group and selects its row. prefs.info and prefs.appearance include the current section id and category. prefs.search {query} returns matches, each with id and category, in sidebar order, except that system ranks Software first. It uses the same search as the sidebar and leaves the window alone. prefs.email, prefs.email.set and prefs.email.password are described under Apps → Email above. prefs.execute {id} runs any command a button or menu would (apps.check, apps.install, appearance.apply, appearance.revert, …), and prefs.actions lists them with their enablement. The window is drivable like every MixOS app (prefs.ui.*, prefs.window). The commands are registered in docs/docs/spec/bus/commands.conf.mix.

For scripted work, call the services directly (releases.*, settings.*): Preferences is their window, not a second implementation.

Wallpaper

Open Wallpaper from Appearance, then choose the default or an output, then Theme, Colour or Image. Colour accepts a picker or #RRGGBB. Browse opens the native image browser at the installed wallpaper folder, or Pictures in your home folder. It lists PNG/JPEG files and folders without blocking the window. Changes stay in Preferences until Apply wallpaper. Revert wallpaper drops them; Refresh wallpaper reads the current state again.

An output's Use default removes just that override. Editing the default preserves every output override. Images currently crop to fill; fit controls and slideshows will follow when backdrop supports them.

Without Backdrop on the session Bus, Wallpaper shows an unavailable page state and creates no problem links. Local edit refusals stay on Wallpaper. A refusal of a submitted apply shows its reason, keeps the draft and leaves the last good wallpaper in place. Preferences checks for intervening changes before sending the whole document; conflicts require Revert and a fresh edit. This check is best effort: backdrop does not yet provide an atomic compare-and-set operation. A lost reply is checked by a state read, never automatically resent.

Wallpaper and browser state are included in prefs.info, wallpaper state in prefs.appearance. Commands wallpaper.apply, wallpaper.revert, wallpaper.refresh and wallpaper.browse are available through prefs.execute; the normal prefs.ui.* commands drive the controls and browser.

Running and testing

Run with prefs [--noded-url URL]; a second launch raises the first window (prefs.show). The Bus connection is citizen.

The source is apps/prefs:

PathWhat
crates/preferencesthe headless engine: sections, rows, notes, one operation at a time, the prefs.* commands
crates/preferences/src/navigation.rsthe section registry, page registry, software groups and search
crates/preferences/src/appearance.rsAppearance: the look, families, scale, density and motion, with drafts, fenced applies and receipts for lost replies
crates/preferences/src/email.rsApps → Email: account changes planned and checked, fenced applies, passwords handed to Email
src/commands.rsevery action as a registered command (menus, buttons, shortcuts, prefs.execute)
src/view.rsthe egui rendering; returns what the person did
src/shell.rsevents in, effects out, in order; drained shutdown
i18n/en/prefs.ftlthe strings

Test with cargo test -p preferences -p prefs. Regenerate the snapshots with UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 and look at the images before committing them.

Macro Bus commands

The shared macro Bus surface uses this process's catalogue and runner. Subscribe to <service>.macros.finished for completion, where service is the instance’s registered Bus name (for example term-1234 for a second Term instance). Commands keep the app’s canonical prefix, such as prefs.macros.run.

CommandArgumentsResult
prefs.macros.list{}Catalogue and diagnostics
prefs.macros.reload{}Catalogue and diagnostics
prefs.macros.run{id}Acceptance and run number
prefs.macros.status{}Current or last run
prefs.macros.output{}Retained output and dropped flag
prefs.macros.stop{}Whether termination was requested
prefs.macros.new{title}Create a user per-app macro; {id,title,path,scanned}, without opening an editor; scan failures add warning and preserve the file
